sources.note: Introduces GSM8K, 8.5K grade-school math word problems, and shows that training a verifier to rank many sampled solutions beats finetuning the generator directly.
sources.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems

sources.note: Bootstraps a model's reasoning ability from a handful of rationale examples by generating rationales, keeping only those that reach the right answer, and finetuning on them in a loop.
sources.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

sources.note: Reaches test-time scaling with two simple ingredients: supervised finetuning on 1,000 curated reasoning traces, and 'budget forcing', which controls thinking length by cutting generation off or appending 'Wait' to extend it.
sources.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling

sources.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
sources.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

sources.note: Builds a large standardized meta-benchmark and finds that LLM-judge preference scores do not correlate with concrete measures of safety, world knowledge or instruction following, because judges systematically prioritize style over factuality and safety.
sources.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking

sources.note: Edits the internal representation of a written scratchpad state while holding the printed text fixed, and asks whether the next step follows the transition rule applied to the edited value — turning 'does the model use its scratchpad?' into a causal test with a single correct answer.
sources.title: Do Models Read What They Write? Causal Registers in Scratchpad Reasoning

result.definition: Training on input-output pairs, and in these sources specifically on reasoning traces. What they collectively show is how little of it is needed and how much depends on which traces: one bootstraps by finetuning only on self-generated rationales that reached correct answers and iterating the loop; one finetunes on 1,000 curated examples selected for difficulty, diversity and quality and beats a much stronger closed model on competition mathematics; and one uses it as the baseline that verifier-based reranking outperforms, reporting that verification scales better with added data than finetuning does. Elsewhere in the archive the same lever runs in reverse — 800 examples suffice to remove a behaviour and halve accuracy — which is the strongest evidence that what it transfers here is substantially stylistic conditioning rather than knowledge. In two further entries it is pipeline background rather than an object of study: the stage at which contamination is introduced before a later RL run conceals it, and the training that precedes the judge behaviour a meta-benchmark then measures.
